fact: Starlink has no official authorisation in Cameroon; its licence application has sat unresolved for over two years, and the regulator ART declined comment, saying the file is with the ministry MINPOSTEL (NewsWatch, 27 July 2026).

In 2024 the government banned Starlink and a Customs circular of 15 April 2024 ordered seizure of Starlink terminal kits at the borders as escaping ART oversight; the article says the circular remains operative.
Customs seized 10 Starlink modems at the Nkometou checkpoint on 12 December 2025 as unauthorised equipment.
Starlink is described as technically banned in Cameroon since April 2024, with systematic customs seizure ordered, and SpaceX suspended service for users in April 2024 after government warnings.

As of the article, ART had finalised a draft concession convention and specifications for Starlink Cameroun SARL, passed to the technical supervisory ministry for possible grant; no licence granted yet.

ART has finalised the draft concession convention and specifications for Starlink Cameroun SARL, passed to the technical supervisory ministry in late November 2025 for possible grant; Starlink is only in position to obtain formal authorisation, none yet issued.

Starlink announced stopping its services in Cameroon in April 2024 for lack of official authorisation and suspended access for Cameroonian users after the government demanded blocking of the grey-market use.

Cameroon has for now refused to grant Starlink a licence and officially prohibited its operation, per the article of 8 March 2025 (its internal dates point to April 2024 events); a Customs note of 15 April ordered systematic seizure of Starlink kits.
Cameroon is among 16 countries Starlink's availability map lists as 'Starting in 2026', which the article says indicates service coverage or regulatory authorisation pending; no launch date given.

Starlink disconnected its service in Cameroon at the end of April 2024 after a government order; the regulator said it operated without a licence and threatened national security and fair competition.

Cameroon customs seized Starlink kits at its borders because Starlink had no licence in Cameroon, and Starlink planned to stop service there on 30 April 2024; customs said seizures continue until the telecoms regulator licenses it.
Cameroon is named among countries that block or restrict Starlink to guard national security and data sovereignty; undated, so the article's publication date is used.
Cameroon authorities banned the import of Starlink kits in April 2024 and ordered the company to cease operations, citing no licence and national security risks.

The Independent (Uganda) reports that Cameroon has held back authorisation for Starlink and has imposed delays or restrictions over regulatory and ownership requirements; no licence is stated (article date used, no other given).

El Pais quotes an analyst saying Cameroon forced Starlink to cease operations earlier in 2024 for lack of a licence, even ordering seizure of Starlink equipment at its ports (month not given; year taken from the article).
